nodes.name: Weekdays 09:00 and 14:00
nodes.notes: Twice a weekday rather than once. The CRM caps the day; running twice spreads the allowance across working hours instead of emptying it in one burst at 09:00, which looks less automated. Raise maxPerCollection in CRM Settings if you want more per run.

nodes.name: Collect approved drafts
nodes.notes: Returns only what the CRM's daily cap allows, with suppression re-checked at this moment and AI content safeguards enforced. A draft handed out here is NEVER offered again — if this workflow dies before sending, that message goes unsent rather than being mailed twice.

nodes.name: Recipient looks deliverable
nodes.notes: Belt and braces. The CRM already validated the address; this stops a malformed value reaching the MTA and producing a hard bounce, which costs reputation.

nodes.name: Pace between sends
nodes.notes: Smooth the queue rather than dumping the allowance at once. At this volume there is no advantage to concurrency, and a burst of similar messages is a spam signature.

nodes.name: Send via own SMTP
nodes.notes: YOUR OWN MTA on your own dedicated domain — Postfix/Exim or cPanel, on a host whose AUP permits this. NOT an ESP free tier: Brevo, Mailjet, Resend, SendGrid, Mailgun, SMTP2GO, Elastic Email, MailerSend, Mailtrap, SES, Postmark and ZeptoMail all prohibit cold outreach in their acceptable-use policies, and Gmail's program policies prohibit unsolicited commercial mail too. Let the MTA own queueing, retries and DSNs; this node only submits. The error output feeds the bounce reporter.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ providerMessageId: $json.messageId || null, sentAt: new Date().toISOString() }) }}

nodes.name: Confirm sent
nodes.notes: This is what moves the lead to CONTACTED and what the daily cap counts — confirmations are the ground truth, not collections. Idempotent on draft id, so a retry after a timeout is not a second send. If this call fails the message was still sent; re-running it is safe.

nodes.name: Report failure
nodes.notes: A hard bounce suppresses the address permanently and moves the lead to NO_CONTACT. Without this nothing ever learns an address is dead and every future campaign retries it, which is how sending reputation is lost. Change kind to 'soft' for temporary failures — a full mailbox is not a reason to stop contacting a business forever. Asynchronous DSNs that arrive later at your MTA should POST here too.
